To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) The E-commerce implementation in Indian MSMEs is still at a nascent stage and is yet to realize its full potential, (ii) The E-commerce adoption by MSMEs is a complex process and is influenced by multiple internal and external factors, (iii) The organizational factors such as top management support, perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use and perceived ease of adoption are found to be significantly influencing the E-Commerce Implementation process.
E-commerce has the potential to increase the competitiveness of the Indian MSME sector in the global economy.
The TOE model is useful in explaining the adoption and diffusion of E-Commerce among MSMEs in Indian context.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of E-commerce implementation in Indian MSMEs and its impact on organizational performance.

there are several factors that can affect the adoption and usage of E-commerce by MSME sector in India.
